_comment: Curated lexicon for generate_laicite.py (GitHub issue #14). Matching is accent- and case-insensitive, whole-word, over RAW text (title + OCR + descriptionAI/abstract/tableOfContents) — NOT over lemma_text, because the concordance needs character offsets into readable text and the `documents` subset carries no lemma columns at all. Surface forms are written here WITH their diacritics for curatorial readability; the generator folds both sides before matching, so 'laïcité' also catches the frequent OCR spelling 'laicite'. Multi-word forms are matched with flexible whitespace and an optional elided article, so 'séparation de l'État et' also catches 'separation de l Etat et'. Edit this file to revise the research instrument — no code change needed.
_membership: MEMBERSHIP RULE (load-bearing, do not widen): an item joins the dossier when it carries the Omeka subject tag 'Laïcité' OR when its text matches a frame listed in `membership_frames`. Every OTHER frame is an annotation computed WITHIN members — never a membership criterion. Widening membership to, say, `ecole` would pull in every education article ever written and the arenas view would silently measure schooling coverage instead of the laïcité contest over schooling.

laicite.note: The juridical-political register the francophone West African press actually argues in.

secularisme.note: Deliberately kept even though it is nearly empty: the sociological register's ABSENCE from the West African press is a publishable finding, and the panel says so rather than hiding the frame.

forms: code des personnes et de la famille

concurrence.note: The pole the Scary Terms block already covers. RE-COUNTED here in the same pass rather than joined from the scary-terms bundles: those bundles are anonymous aggregates carrying no o:id, so they cannot answer 'in WHICH items do laïcité and intégrisme co-occur'. Counting three extra families in a pass that is already running is nearly free and yields the per-item cross-tab the laïcité ↔ intégrisme finding needs.

_disambiguation: The `laïc` / `laïque` FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP. In a corpus with heavy Catholic press coverage these forms ALSO mean 'lay person' (the laity, as opposed to the clergy) — 'les fidèles laïcs', 'l'apostolat des laïcs', 'le laïcat'. That is a different concept from 'laïcité de l'État' and it contaminates counts if matched naively. This is the same class of problem as the `fondamental` / `fondamentalisme` exclusion documented in generate_scary_terms.py, but it cannot be fixed by an exclusion list alone, because the SAME surface form carries both senses. So each ambiguous occurrence is classified by a narrow window: an immediate qualifier decides when present (±2 tokens), otherwise a ±8-token neighbourhood vote. Occurrences classified `laity` are counted and reported but do NOT contribute to frame counts, and never seed dossier membership on their own. Measured demotion rates when this file was written: documents 2.9%, publications 2.4%, articles 2.9%, references 8.0% — references being highest because the scholarly corpus discusses Catholic lay movements directly. Spot-checked precision on both sides was high but not perfect; the counts are logged by the generator and surfaced in laicite-metadata.json so the decision stays auditable and tunable here rather than in code.
_stopwords_en: The IWAC corpus is BILINGUAL where it is scholarly: `references` carries English-language work on secularism, and a handful of articles are in English. iwac_utils.STOPWORDS is French-only, so without this list the English function words rank as top 'collocates' of any English-heavy slice — the first run of the 2020s decade slice returned literally `that, this, religious, with, from`, which measures the language of recent scholarship rather than anything about the 2020s. These are function words only: no content term, and nothing from the Islamic-domain research vocabulary the repo's CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids filtering (COSIM, FAIB, UIB, Ramadan, Tabaski, Maouloud and friends are research terms, not noise, in either language).
_ocr_noise: Tokens that are artefacts of digitisation rather than of the text: scanning-app watermarks stamped onto every page of a scan. These are NOT domain filtering — a watermark is not vocabulary. `camscanner` reached the top of the first collocate run because one repeatedly-scanned periodical stamped it on every page. The document-frequency floor in the generator catches most such cases on its own; this list handles the ones that appear across many documents because the same scanner produced them.
_authority: The concept carries a curated Omeka authority record — index o:id 5, 'Laïcité', Type 'Sujets'. Two Événements records hang off it: 193 (Forum national sur la laïcité, Burkina Faso) and 224 (Colloque national sur les confessions religieuses et laïcité, Benin). The generator links to all three and cross-checks the subject label against the index at run time.
